reason: The cited evidence discusses thermal conductivity mechanisms in concentrated alloys (E1), irradiation tolerance in HEAs (E2), and properties of W-based HEAs (E3), but none provides specific support for the key premises about interfacial electron scattering in W–Cu composites, the effect of a coating on that scattering, or the coating's stability under relevant conditions.
premises: Interfacial electron scattering limits thermal conductivity in W–Cu composites
An ultra-thin high-conductivity coating on W can reduce electron scattering at the interface
Reducing interfacial electron scattering increases the electronic contribution to thermal conductivity
An ultra-thin coating will not degrade mechanical durability or irradiation resistance
